Kamyanka-Buzka Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · L'vivs'ka oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Kamyanka-Buzka's Jewish community, first documented in 1465, received the right to purchase houses and engage in trade in 1589, and permission to build a synagogue in 1627. In 1837, Sholom Rosenfeld (1800–1852) founded a Hasidic dynasty in the town. The population reached a peak of 3,142 (48.4 percent of the town) in 1890. On September 15, 1942, around 1,500 Jews were deported to the Bełżec death camp. This is the older of Kamyanka-Buzka's cemeteries; a cinema and publishing house now stand on its western part, with a public park on the eastern part.
